paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Yiwu, in Yunnan, made from leaf dated to 2008. That leaf had already been aging before it was pressed, so the cake started further along than one pressed from fresh material. It was made by the [wet-pile method](shou:wet-piling), which Yunnan’s factories brought into production in 1973.
At eighteen years, it belongs to what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). Storage shapes a tea like this as much as the years do.

brewing.text: Ease a piece off the cake along its edge with a pick rather than snapping it. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. Ripe tea like this gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A smooth, deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
